To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
Notch activation stimulates migration and proliferation of transformed mammary epithelial cells and promotes tumor progression.

1) Notch activation stimulates migration and invasiveness of breast cancer cells, which is correlated with E-Cadherin reduction and delocalisation; 2) Notch activation in MCF- 7 breast cancer cell line promotes tumorigenesis and growth in vivo, and 3) Notch activation causes the formation of papillar tumors in vivo, which show increased expression of Hes1 and delocalization and reduction of E-cadherins.
Notch activation in MCF-10A cells induces EMT and that the effect of Notch on cell invasion is cell type specific.
In summary, our research is concerned with
studying the role of the Notch pathway in breast cancer, and the molecular mechanisms involved.
understanding the molecular and cellular mechanisms involved in the initiation, progression and metastasis of breast cancer and the development of novel therapeutic strategies.
the study of the role of Notch signaling during the development of breast tumors, and the identification of the factors involved in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Notch1 activation is associated to increased tumor growth in breast cancer cells.
NOTCH1 activation promotes the growth of breast tumors in a context-dependent manner.
Notch signaling is a critical regulator of the EMT process in epithelial cancer, and thus a potential therapeutic target for breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NOTCH signaling has context-dependent roles during breast cancer progression.
Notch activation in breast epithelial cells promotes tumor growth by inducing epithelial-mesenquimal transition and by promoting cell migration.

Notch activation stimulates migration and invasion of breast cancer cells, and that this effect is mediated by the loss of E-Cadherin expression and localization, and the consequent increase in cell motility.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Notch signaling is involved in the progression of breast tumors and that the Notch pathway is a potential target for breast cancer therapy.
Notch activation is a signal triggering epithelia mesenchymal transition (EMT), which has implications in tumor dissemination and metastasis, and in tumor proliferation in vivo.
Notch1 activation is a signal that promotes breast cancer progression, and this is mediated in part through the downregulation of the epithelial cell marker, E-Cadherin.
